P9.text: Plain `const b = a` / `let b = a` of a heap value (array, map, struct) makes b another name for a's object while b stays local: writes through a or b show in both, with no copy and no retain-split, as in TypeScript. Reassigning a whole name never changes the object (`let saved = a; a = []` keeps saved on the old array, TypeScript's result). The snippet compiles and synonym.length is 3 after the push. Soundness rule: b is local only if it is not returned, stored in a struct, array, map or Cell, captured by an escaping closure or sent to a thread; otherwise a later write to a is still E0978 with the fix copy(a). Writes through an alias group use an in-place write with no copy-on-write check, because the checker proves every other holder is a group member. No new heap edge exists, so J5 holds; nothing crosses a thread, so J6 holds. Every program accepted today keeps its meaning: the new rule only changes programs that are E0978 today.

O12.text: Escape is decidable in one function body only by being flow-insensitive: b escaping anywhere (a return after the write, a store, an escaping capture) must make the whole group escaping, so the E0978 appears at an earlier write, far from the escape. Across calls it is undecidable without markers: `foo(b)` may store b through a mutable parameter (a known gap) and `const c = f(b)` shares only if f has `from`. Branches also make group size flow-dependent: `let b = a; if (c) { b = other }` leaves b in the group on one path only, so the emitter needs the group per path, and a loop body that writes `let b = a` each iteration builds a new group per pass. Generators and `for ... of` iterators hold the place they walk, so a group member can be a hidden iterator. None of this is in the 850k estimate.
